lessons.title: Run and inspect a program
lessons.objective: Edit and commit a Python file in github.dev, inspect its GitHub Actions output, and distinguish source from execution.
lessons.github_task: Edit workspace/main.py in github.dev, Commit & Push, and open the matching Run Python lesson result.
lessons.github_evidence: Explain the printed result and identify the source file, commit, and Actions output.

lessons.title: Values names and arithmetic
lessons.objective: Trace assignments and use integers, floats, strings, booleans, and `None` for appropriate purposes.
lessons.github_task: Change the arithmetic in your Python file, inspect the old and new lines in Source Control, and commit the change.
lessons.github_evidence: Show the arithmetic prediction, the diff, and the result for that commit.

lessons.title: Strings and text transformations
lessons.objective: Index, slice, normalize, combine, and format simple text.
lessons.github_task: Commit one string-cleaning change with a message explaining its behavior, and inspect its Actions output.
lessons.github_evidence: Connect the changed expression with the output and the commit message.

lessons.title: Input conversion and explicit contracts
lessons.objective: Distinguish text input, conversion, and a program's validity rules.
lessons.github_task: Commit the program and one answer per prompt in workspace/input.txt, then inspect the same run.
lessons.github_evidence: Explain which input line was converted and show the observed conversion result or error.

lessons.title: Booleans decisions and boundaries
lessons.objective: Express a decision with comparisons and test all its boundaries.
lessons.github_task: Change sample inputs to exercise the decision boundaries and commit the cases with your Python code.
lessons.github_evidence: Link the tested boundary cases to the committed inputs and output.

lessons.title: Loops accumulation and termination
lessons.objective: Trace and write finite repetition, including an empty input.
lessons.github_task: Run a finite loop in Actions, inspect its output, and locate Cancel workflow before trying termination repairs.
lessons.github_evidence: Explain the stopping condition and distinguish a finished run from a cancelled or timed-out run.

lessons.title: Collections and choosing a representation
lessons.objective: Choose and use a list, tuple, dictionary, or set for a small task.
lessons.github_task: Commit a collection change and inspect which list or dictionary entries changed in the diff.
lessons.github_evidence: Explain both the representation choice and what the commit actually records.

lessons.title: Functions parameters and return values
lessons.objective: Turn a computation into a reusable function with an explicit contract.
lessons.github_task: Create a function-change branch in the browser, refactor your calculation, commit it, and open a PR.
lessons.github_evidence: Show the function result and identify the PR base, head, and Python diff before merging.

lessons.title: References mutation and scope
lessons.objective: Explain aliasing, a shallow copy, a mutable default, and local rebinding.
lessons.github_task: On your practice branch, inspect a mutation-related change and review exactly which lines you stage.
lessons.github_evidence: Predict the object behavior and connect the staged diff to the resulting commit.

lessons.title: Errors debugging and tests
lessons.objective: Reproduce a failure, read a traceback, repair its cause, and test the repair.
lessons.github_task: Use the failing Actions traceback to fix a Python bug, add a regression test in workspace/test_*.py, and inspect a new run.
lessons.github_evidence: Link the failing and repaired commits; explain the test that detects the bug.

lessons.title: Modules environments and standard tools
lessons.objective: Import a helper without starting its interactive interface and identify which interpreter owns an installed package.
lessons.github_task: Commit a helper and its import together; use the hosted environment exercise in the browser workflow guide.
lessons.github_evidence: Show the import result and identify the interpreter reported by the workflow.

lessons.title: Files serialization and the first project
lessons.objective: Save and load validated practice data without silently discarding a damaged existing file.
lessons.github_task: Deliver the study tracker on a branch with committed sample data, a README, and an inspected PR.
lessons.github_evidence: Show save-and-reopen behavior, the source/run links, and a PR explanation of the independent feature.

lessons.title: Collection patterns and complexity
lessons.objective: Choose clear collection operations and explain their main time and space tradeoffs.
lessons.github_task: Review a collection refactor as one focused Python diff with tests before and after.
lessons.github_evidence: Explain unchanged behavior, relevant complexity, and the observed check result.

lessons.title: Iterators generators and streaming
lessons.objective: Consume a stream once and account for its lifetime and storage.
lessons.github_task: Commit a generator and tests for empty and single-use input, then inspect the learner-test log.
lessons.github_evidence: Connect streaming behavior and lifetime checks with the run for that commit.

lessons.title: Function interfaces scope and wrappers
lessons.objective: Design an interface with explicit inputs, defaults, outputs, and mutation.
lessons.github_task: Open a PR for an interface change and explain its caller impact in the description.
lessons.github_evidence: Review a caller diff and demonstrate the revised contract.

lessons.title: Classes dataclasses and composition
lessons.objective: Model useful state without accidental sharing or unnecessary inheritance.
lessons.github_task: Review the class or composition change together with tests for independent instance state.
lessons.github_evidence: Use the PR diff and test output to explain ownership and accidental sharing.

lessons.title: Exceptions and resource ownership
lessons.objective: Preserve useful error context and release resources on failure.
lessons.github_task: Commit a resource-failure test and inspect its error context and cleanup result in Actions.
lessons.github_evidence: Explain the failure boundary using the test and run, not only a success-path example.

lessons.title: Type hints and runtime validation
lessons.objective: Use annotations to communicate interfaces without mistaking them for checks.
lessons.github_task: Add the chosen type checker as a hosted workflow step when needed; compare it with runtime validation tests.
lessons.github_evidence: Identify the distinct static and runtime results for the same Python interface.

lessons.title: Testing debugging and logging
lessons.objective: Connect requirements to tests and diagnose failures with controlled evidence.
lessons.github_task: Add meaningful workspace tests and inspect their discovery count, failure messages, and result in Actions.
lessons.github_evidence: Show a test failing for the intended defect and passing after its fix.

lessons.title: Structured text numbers and dates
lessons.objective: Preserve a data format's meaning through parsing, validation, and output.
lessons.github_task: Commit a small data fixture and document its schema beside the Python parser.
lessons.github_evidence: Review the fixture diff and explain a quoting, date, or numeric boundary test.

lessons.title: HTTP APIs and external failures
lessons.objective: Design a small external-service adapter with bounded failure behavior.
lessons.github_task: Use a recorded GitHub API response to test your Python adapter; run any bounded live read from Actions.
lessons.github_evidence: Distinguish fixture checks from live observations and explain pagination or failure handling.

lessons.title: SQLite queries and transactions
lessons.objective: Store records with parameterized queries and demonstrate transaction behavior.
lessons.github_task: Commit SQLite transaction tests using temporary runner files and inspect rollback evidence.
lessons.github_evidence: Explain the database invariant and link the test run for that code.

lessons.title: Git packaging and reproducible setup
lessons.objective: Make a project installable and explain what a version-control change contains.
lessons.github_task: Build your package in a hosted workflow and use a simple competing-line PR to practice browser conflict resolution.
lessons.github_evidence: Show a fresh runner installation and verify the resolved Python behavior.

lessons.title: Algorithms command lines and application delivery
lessons.objective: Deliver a complete small application with a justified algorithm and usable failures.
lessons.github_task: Finish the report application PR and prepare a GitHub release draft describing its tested command interface.
lessons.github_evidence: Link the reviewed commit, hosted command results, and release notes; a draft is not a publication.

lessons.title: Protocols descriptors and object behavior
lessons.objective: Explain attribute lookup and implement a small, lawful Python protocol.
lessons.github_task: Review a protocol implementation with contract tests as one focused PR.
lessons.github_evidence: Explain protocol behavior using its diff and the Actions test evidence.

lessons.title: Closures decorators and caches
lessons.objective: Preserve a callable's contract and justify any retained state.
lessons.github_task: Commit decorator or cache changes with tests for preserved interfaces and retained state.
lessons.github_evidence: Review the callable contract and invalidation behavior alongside the run.

lessons.title: Advanced typing and API boundaries
lessons.objective: Express meaningful generic relationships without inventing runtime guarantees.
lessons.github_task: Inspect type-checking and runtime-test jobs for the same API change.
lessons.github_evidence: Explain what each check can establish and review the public API diff.

lessons.title: Runtime memory and inspection
lessons.objective: Separate language guarantees from observations about a particular runtime.
lessons.github_task: Record the runner Python version with a small runtime observation in a committed note.
lessons.github_evidence: Distinguish a version-specific observation from a language guarantee and link the run.

lessons.title: Algorithms profiling and fair benchmarks
lessons.objective: Identify a limiting cost and evaluate an optimization without changing the contract.
lessons.github_task: Compare bounded profiling runs for two commits and record workload and runner conditions.
lessons.github_evidence: Report raw measurements and limits without claiming hosted timing proves a universal speedup.

lessons.title: Threads processes and isolated interpreters
lessons.objective: Choose a concurrency mechanism based on work, ownership, and transfer costs.
lessons.github_task: Run bounded concurrency and cleanup tests in Actions and inspect the configured Python version.
lessons.github_evidence: Connect ownership and failure behavior to actual job results.

lessons.title: Async work bounds and cancellation
lessons.objective: Bound a pipeline's tasks, queue, and retained results and prove cleanup.
lessons.github_task: Review async bounds and cancellation tests in the PR and inspect their hosted results.
lessons.github_evidence: Show worker-failure and cancellation evidence for the reviewed commit.

lessons.title: Transactions retries and distributed uncertainty
lessons.objective: Protect an invariant across failures and identify uncertain remote outcomes.
lessons.github_task: Commit a failure scenario and an explanation of uncertain outcomes with the implementation.
lessons.github_evidence: Link rollback or retry tests to the stated invariant and documented limits.

lessons.title: Architecture security and operations
lessons.objective: Make a system's rules, dependencies, and failure signals understandable.
lessons.github_task: Review workflow permissions and an architecture change alongside its Python trust boundaries.
lessons.github_evidence: Explain which code and tools can access which resources without claiming an unverified setting.

lessons.title: Reliable delivery and specialization
lessons.objective: Deliver an expert-level project with independent evidence and a clear specialty route.
lessons.github_task: Deliver the bounded-system capstone with a reviewed release candidate and hosted clean-build checks.
lessons.github_evidence: Connect the release candidate to its code, failure tests, and runbook.

lessons.title: Questions literature and scope
lessons.objective: Form a tractable question and distinguish evidence gaps from unfamiliarity.
lessons.github_task: Commit a research question and protocol beside the planned Python experiment before collecting final results.
lessons.github_evidence: Point to the protocol commit and distinguish hypotheses from established findings.

lessons.title: Mathematical and numerical validity
lessons.objective: Identify the mathematical assumptions and numerical errors relevant to a result.
lessons.github_task: Run small numerical checks in the recorded hosted environment and commit their assumptions.
lessons.github_evidence: Explain tolerances using observed residuals and reference cases.

lessons.title: Experimental units baselines and uncertainty
lessons.objective: Design a comparison whose uncertainty analysis matches its sampling units.
lessons.github_task: Review the experiment design and paired-data checks in the same PR as the Python analysis.
lessons.github_evidence: Identify experimental units, baseline, uncertainty method, and code evidence.

lessons.title: Reproducibility provenance and randomness
lessons.objective: Regenerate a result from recorded inputs, code, configuration, and environment.
lessons.github_task: Record exact commit, seed, dependencies, configuration, and result-retention method for a hosted rerun.
lessons.github_evidence: Demonstrate reproducibility within the stated environment and identify missing evidence.

lessons.title: Verification validation and scientific tests
lessons.objective: Test whether the implementation follows its specification and whether the specification supports the intended investigation.
lessons.github_task: Review scientific invariants and validation assumptions with the experiment code and CI result.
lessons.github_evidence: Explain which checks test implementation and which address the scientific model.

lessons.title: Performance scaling and computational budgets
lessons.objective: Evaluate computational cost under equivalent accuracy and workload conditions.
lessons.github_task: Record a bounded hosted workload and compute budget before running a scaling comparison.
lessons.github_evidence: Compare equivalent workloads and report shared-runner measurement limits.

lessons.title: Scientific communication and critique
lessons.objective: Write a report in which claims, methods, results, and limits can be inspected.
lessons.github_task: Commit the methods and results report with permanent links to code and observed runs.
lessons.github_evidence: Make each key claim traceable to data, method, and a stated limitation.

lessons.title: Replication and the research capstone
lessons.objective: Complete one bounded investigation with reproducible evidence and an honest conclusion.
lessons.github_task: Deliver the investigation through a reviewed PR with reproduction instructions using GitHub Actions.
lessons.github_evidence: Record an independent rerun if observed; label a self-rerun accurately.

lessons.title: Contribution value and novelty
lessons.objective: Define a worthwhile contribution without confusing novelty, complexity, and usefulness.
lessons.github_task: Define a bounded contribution in a GitHub document and review the evidence behind the proposed Python change.
lessons.github_evidence: State the intended benefit, existing alternatives, and the exact contribution scope.

lessons.title: Public APIs and compatibility
lessons.objective: Design an interface other people can use and evolve without hidden assumptions.
lessons.github_task: Review compatibility tests and design decisions together in a focused Python PR.
lessons.github_evidence: Explain which users or callers are affected using the diff and observed checks.

lessons.title: Prototypes baselines and decision records
lessons.objective: Use a small prototype to compare alternatives and decide whether to continue.
lessons.github_task: Compare the candidate and baseline at recorded commits using hosted evaluation jobs.
lessons.github_evidence: Keep raw evidence, negative results, and limits tied to code versions.

lessons.title: Language runtime and tool creation
lessons.objective: Investigate one language/tooling problem with a defined supported subset.
lessons.github_task: For an optional interpreter contribution, inspect upstream browser guidance and prepare a scoped change with hosted checks.
lessons.github_evidence: Distinguish an inspected proposal from an accepted or released upstream feature.

lessons.title: Scientific native and systems contributions
lessons.objective: Define the extra domain and interoperability evidence needed by a chosen specialty.
lessons.github_task: For an optional scientific-system change, review bounded hosted integration checks and ownership assumptions.
lessons.github_evidence: Link the experiment configuration and observed results to the proposed implementation.

lessons.title: Independent evaluation and adversarial review
lessons.objective: Evaluate a contribution under conditions that can reveal its weaknesses.
lessons.github_task: Prepare the useful-contribution release candidate with browser reproduction instructions and linked checks.
lessons.github_evidence: Show first-use evidence and clearly distinguish draft, publication, and independent feedback.

lessons.title: Releases community and governance
lessons.objective: Prepare a reviewable release or upstream change that respects its destination.
lessons.github_task: Commit maintenance guidance and review a small follow-up Python fix through the same browser workflow.
lessons.github_evidence: Explain triage, compatibility, account boundaries, and regression evidence.

lessons.title: Maintenance mentoring and the creator capstone
lessons.objective: Make a useful contribution understandable and maintainable beyond its creator.
lessons.github_task: Finish the capstone with a reviewed maintenance and recovery plan tied to your Python deliverable.
lessons.github_evidence: Explain what was demonstrated, what remains unverified, and the next useful contribution.

lessons.title: Read your Python repository
lessons.objective: Locate the current Python lesson, practice file, branch, history, and run on GitHub.

lessons.title: Complete a browser pull request
lessons.objective: Use a branch and pull request to review a change to your current Python function.

lessons.title: Use github.dev and hosted Python execution
lessons.objective: Distinguish browser editing, GitHub sign-in, repository access, and hosted execution.

lessons.title: Review and commit Python snapshots
lessons.objective: Explain which Python edits are included in a commit by inspecting the browser diff.

lessons.title: Keep browser branches current
lessons.objective: Identify the branch versions used by a Python change and prepare a current browser branch.

lessons.title: Review contributions and choose a merge method
lessons.objective: Review the Python contract, diff, and observed checks before incorporating a contribution.

lessons.title: Resolve a conflict and verify the combined result
lessons.objective: Resolve a simple competing-line Python conflict through GitHub and test the intended result.

lessons.title: Recover a Python change in the browser
lessons.objective: Restore intended Python behavior with a reviewable new change and preserve useful history.

lessons.title: Review a small Python change with real tests
lessons.objective: Connect a Python behavior contract to a regression test that actually executes.

lessons.title: Understand and inspect GitHub Actions
lessons.objective: Read the output and status of a hosted run for the current Python commit.

lessons.title: Find work and document it clearly
lessons.objective: Use GitHub search and Markdown to make a Python task or result understandable.

lessons.title: Protect accounts and review boundaries
lessons.objective: Relate repository access and workflow permissions to the Python code being executed.

lessons.title: Release useful work and understand usage limits
lessons.objective: Tie a release candidate to tested Python behavior and a bounded hosted workflow.

lessons.title: Read GitHub APIs from Python
lessons.objective: Apply Python HTTP and JSON skills to a bounded read-only GitHub API example.

lessons.title: Collaborate with a tutor or coding agent
lessons.objective: Give an assistant a bounded Python task and inspect its actual repository work.

lessons.title: Maintain history and test a restoration plan
lessons.objective: Use GitHub history and hosted reproduction to preserve an inspectable Python result.
